changes.current_line: Built for developers: launch payments fast with our APIs, docs and sandbox.
changes.change: For engineering-led marketplace prospects, make the proof hands-on: 'Your engineers can build a working payment flow for your sellers in our sandbox over a weekend.' Back it in the sales motion by getting their engineers into the sandbox in week one, rather than leaving it to chance.
changes.why: The deal turned when a customer engineer built 'a working sitter payment flow over a weekend' on our docs and sandbox, and after that Daniel 'stopped saying 'if''.

changes.current_line: Financial infrastructure to grow globally, in every currency.
changes.change: For engineering-led marketplace prospects, open with the engineering burden: 'Payments shouldn't be a team.' Stop babysitting your payments code and give that engineering time back to your roadmap. Treat new-country launches as the occasion, not the headline.
changes.why: Expansion set the timing, but the buyer's own words ('haunted house', 'We want to stop babysitting this', 'Payments shouldn't be a team') and two engineers working on payments more or less full-time show the real pain was upkeep, not global reach.

changes.current_line: Customers see an average uplift in authorization rates with Authorization Boost and Adaptive Acceptance.
changes.change: Stop leading with the acceptance-rate slide for engineering-led marketplace buyers whose pain is maintenance. Keep it available if they raise authorization rates themselves.
changes.why: The acceptance-rate slide met silence, and the decision-maker dismissed it outright: 'I'm not losing sleep over auth rates.'

changes.current_line: Onboard, verify and pay out to sellers worldwide, in their local currency.
changes.change: For marketplace prospects, use the buyer's terms instead of 'payouts' and 'marketplace'. Example: 'Onboard and verify your sitters, and handle sitter pay locally in each new country.' Then answer when sellers get paid, because buyers frame pay timing as a promise (here, 'paid by Friday'). Product must confirm what pay timing we can support before any timing claim goes in the line.
changes.why: The marketplace capabilities landed, but the customer says 'sitter pay', not 'payouts', and both the promise to sitters ('paid by Friday') and the CFO's only question ('does this change when sitters get paid?') were about pay timing, which no current line addresses.
